# WP-01 Closeout — Repository, Schemas, Constants, Vector Harness and CI Bootstrap

**Work package:** WP-01 (EDP §7)
**Baseline:** SRS v1.1 / TRS v1.1 / EDP v1.0
**Machine-readable results:** [`closeout-results.json`](closeout-results.json) — generated by
`go run ./tools/closeout`, derived from `evidence/trace/trace-matrix.json`. Every number in this
document comes from that file. The generator reads status and never writes it.

This is a **frozen record of one moment**. WP-02 will move statuses; this document must not be
edited to keep pace with them. `generated_for_commit` in the JSON names the tree it describes, and
`tools/closeout` asserts by test that this document and that JSON agree with each other — not with
a matrix that has since moved on.

### 2.1 What the run covers

Two workflows gate every pull request, and both run in full here.

**`conformance.yml`** — four test runners over the **same committed vector files**, then the
traceability gate:

| Runner | Host | What it consumes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `go conformance` | ubuntu | `go test ./...`, plus `gofmt`, `go vet`, `constantsgen -check`, `vectorgen -check` |
| `java conformance` | ubuntu | pure-JVM `:protocol-conformance`, JUnit 5, no Android framework |
| `swift conformance + iOS shell` | macos-latest | `LumosProtocolConformance` (XCTest) and `LumosAppShell`, the latter also compiled for `arm64-apple-ios17.0` |
| `admin console tests` | ubuntu | `node:test`, junit-reported |
| `traceability gate` | ubuntu | TRS §19.3 completeness, freshness and status honesty against the executed-test set |

**`pipeline.yml`** — lint, secret scan, dependency locks, SBOM and the four shell builds.

### 2.2 The complete §18.4 vector suite

12 vector files plus the manifest and README, all emitted by `tools/vectorgen` and consumed by
every runner. `tools/vectorgen` is the **only** writer; Java and Swift consume only.

```
test-vectors/manifest.json
test-vectors/framing/frame_roundtrip.json      test-vectors/framing/frame_invalid.json
test-vectors/crypto/x3dh_kat.json              test-vectors/crypto/ratchet_sequences.json
test-vectors/crypto/aead_kat.json              test-vectors/crypto/safety_number.json
test-vectors/adv/ble_advertisement.json        test-vectors/media/object_pipeline.json
test-vectors/config/package_valid.json         test-vectors/config/package_invalid.json
test-vectors/voucher/voucher_tokens.json       test-vectors/errors/error_codes.json
```

Two gates guard the suite itself, both green:

- **Determinism self-check** — `vectorgen` builds the whole suite twice and byte-compares before
  writing. `vectorgen -check` re-runs it against the committed files.
- **`constants_hash` cross-check** — every vector file embeds the register hash; `constantsgen
  -check` proves the 14 generated artefacts still match `lumos_constants.json`.

A **missing vector file is a failed gate**, not a skipped test (`assertSuiteComplete`).

### 3.1 Why the nine `implemented` rows are not `tested`

`implemented` here means the mechanism exists and is exercised, but the requirement's own
verification method has not been performed. Each is a deliberate hold, not an oversight.

| ID | Held because |
| --- | --- |
| TRS-CICD-001 | Verification is "pipeline inspection" — a reviewer's act, not a test's. All six mandated stages exist and run. |
| TRS-CICD-005 | Schema versioning exists; **compatibility** testing across versions needs a second version to compare against. |
| TRS-CONST-002 | Bounds validation is register-derived and tested, but the requirement's "negative config suite" covers signed packages a client actually rejects at runtime — no client exists. |
| TRS-CONST-003 | The change-control loop (regenerate vectors + full conformance rerun) is enforceable but has never been exercised by an actual frozen-constant change. |
| TRS-PROTO-009 | Verification is **radio capture**. Owner-executed (G-01). The 18-byte layout, authTag derivation and EID schedule are vector-tested; the radio is not. |
| TRS-REP-004 | The four-variant mechanism exists on all four platforms, but there are no endpoints, keys or logging behaviour to separate yet. The Android flavours have no test source asserting them — a real gap for WP-02. |
| TRS-REP-005 | Verification is "secret scan". It runs over full history with a liveness canary, but a CI gate is not a collected test and cannot back a `tested` row under §19.3. |
| TRS-REP-006 | Verification is a **fresh-machine setup test**. The scripts are tested for internal consistency; nobody has run them on a clean host. |
| TRS-REP-007 | The backend, iOS shell and admin console report provenance and are tested. **Release artefacts** (APK/IPA) carrying version + protocol version + config-key-set version is not wired. |

## 4. Deviations, ADR drafts raised and owner decisions

### 4.1 ADRs raised during implementation (TRS-AI-006)

ADR-001..004 are baselined in the EDP. ADR-005..009 were raised by the implementing agent when the
documents left a genuine ambiguity, and **all five were ratified by the owner** before the work
depending on them merged.

| ADR | Subject | Status | What it resolved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [005](../../docs/adrs/ADR-005-safety-number-format.md) | `SAFETY_NUMBER_FORMAT` | **Accepted** | The seed left the format unspecified. Frozen at **60 digits + 6 emoji** (total, not 12) from a fixed 64-glyph alphabet. |
| [006](../../docs/adrs/ADR-006-override-bounds.md) | Override bounds | **Accepted** | TRS §23 marked 11 constants overridable **without stating bounds**, so TRS-CONST-002 was unenforceable. Owner supplied a normative bound for each; `bounds_unspecified` is now cleared everywhere and pinned by test. |
| [007](../../docs/adrs/ADR-007-wire-encoding-choices.md) | Wire encodings | **Accepted** | TRS §9.1 named a version byte and flag field without fixing their encoding. Frozen: high nibble major / low nibble minor (v1.0 = `0x10`); four flag bit positions with `0xFFF0` reserved. |
| [008](../../docs/adrs/ADR-008-identity-dh-key.md) | Separate X25519 identity-DH key | **Accepted, 2 conditions** | ADR-001's mandated libraries expose no Ed25519↔X25519 conversion, so X3DH cannot use the Ed25519 identity key directly. A separate X25519 key, Ed25519-signed. **Both conditions enforced by test**: Ed25519 remains the sole root of trust (safety number and SRS-IDN-006 re-verification key on it alone), and signature verification **fails closed before any DH**, pinned by a negative vector with its exact error code. |
| [009](../../docs/adrs/ADR-009-safety-number-emoji-alphabet.md) | The 64-emoji alphabet | **Accepted** | ADR-005 required a curated alphabet. Selection criteria are **security criteria**, not aesthetic: cross-platform font survival and non-confusability. |

**Two flags carried forward, both to gate G-07 (owner-commissioned cryptographic review):**

- **ADR-008** — a separate identity-DH key is a deviation from the plain X3DH construction and is
  exactly the kind of change an external reviewer must see. The G-07 flag is retained deliberately.
- **ADR-009** — the alphabet's non-confusability property was reasoned about, not **human-tested**.
  Nobody has sat two people in front of two devices and asked whether they can tell the glyphs
  apart. That is a human-factors check no agent can perform.

### 4.3 Toolchain and dependency deviations

Every dependency carries name, version, licence and reason in
`tools/toolchain/toolchain-manifest.json`; `tools/deplock` asserts by test that the manifest still
describes what the lockfiles pin.

| Change | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.54.0 (BSD-3) | ChaCha20-Poly1305 IETF; the Go stdlib has X25519, Ed25519, HKDF and SHA-256 but not this AEAD. **Owner-approved.** No other crypto primitive was added. |
| AGP 8.13.0 → **9.3.1** | 8.13 calls `org.gradle.api.problems.internal.InternalProblems`, removed in Gradle 9.6.0. Bumping AGP beat downgrading the checksum-pinned Gradle 9.7.0 wrapper. |
| Android flavour `test` → **`qa`** | AGP reserves the `test` product-flavour prefix. `LUMOS_ENVIRONMENT` still resolves to `"test"`, so TRS-REP-004's vocabulary survives. |
| Android lint `OldTargetApi`, `GradleDependency` disabled | They demand SDK 37; **TRS §5.3 pins the baseline at 36**. A spec value is a change request, not a lint fix. TRS-CICD-006 owns dependency freshness. |
| Android lint `MissingApplicationIcon` disabled | The shell declares no launchable component. The icon is a WP-10 design deliverable and a placeholder would be exactly the stub AGENTS.md §3 forbids. |
| JUnit 5.11.3 (**EPL-2.0**) | Test-scope only, never distributed. **Flagged explicitly because EPL is copyleft-family**, per the dependency rule. |
| Gson 2.11.0 (Apache-2.0) | The JDK ships no JSON parser and the Java runner must read the committed vectors. |
| eslint 9.15.0 → **9.39.5**, `@types/node` 22 → 24 | Two **low** ReDoS advisories (GHSA-xffm-g5w8-qvg7) in the transitive `@eslint/plugin-kit`; node types moved to match the pinned runtime. ESLint 10 deliberately **not** taken: major bump, no security motive. |
| gitleaks 8.30.1 (MIT) | Full-history secret scan. Licence read from the LICENSE file in the installed package, not assumed. |
| Python 3.14.5 + pypdf | **Authoring host only**, used to read the baselined PDFs. Explicitly excluded from every lockfile and bootstrap script. |

### 4.4 Scope judgments

- **`test-vectors/` is written by `tools/vectorgen` alone.** Java and Swift consume. This
  single-generator rule (TRS §18.4) held for the whole work package.
- **`admin-console` tests run in `conformance.yml`, not beside their shell build in
  `pipeline.yml`.** The traceability gate can only download artefacts from its own workflow run; a
  test executed in another workflow cannot support a `tested` status however green it is.
- **The iOS shell rides the existing macOS job** rather than a second one — same SwiftPM package,
  and macOS minutes are billed at a premium.
- **No `-check` gate on this closeout.** A closeout is a frozen record; a CI gate holding it to a
  moving matrix would force it to be rewritten until it no longer described the moment it exists to
  describe. It is checked against its own snapshot instead.

## 5. Findings

### 5.1 The closeout's own finding: WP-01 shipped with every Swift identifier broken

Found while assembling this document, by comparing each requirement's linked tests against the
executed set of a real run — the check §3's last column represents. **All 13 Swift identifiers the
matrix links matched nothing**, while the very same run reported `swift: 10 passing tests` and
`swift: 3 passing tests`, and the traceability gate passed.

**Cause, and it is mine.** Slice S7 changed the collector to prefer the `<testsuite>` name over the
testcase `classname`, because `node:test`'s junit reporter writes the literal placeholder
`classname="test"` for every case. SwiftPM does the **mirror image**: one
`<testsuite name="TestResults">` wrapping everything, with the real suite in `classname`. Preferring
the suite name renamed every Swift identifier to `TestResults.<method>`.

**Why nothing complained.** Every affected row also links Go or Java tests that did execute, so
`tested` remained satisfiable. An entire runner's evidence stopped counting and the gate stayed
green. That is the same shape as the S6 defects below — the *third* occurrence — so it is now a rule
rather than a lesson:

> `checkIdentifierShapes` fails when a `lang:module` pair produces executed identifiers this run but
> **none** of the ones the matrix links. Validated against the drifted artefact from run
> `31540270055`, where it reports both Swift modules.

A pair that produces *nothing at all* is deliberately not flagged: that is a legitimately skipped
job (the Swift path filter), and the collector's fail-on-empty rule covers the real case.

**The fixture is why it shipped**, and this is the part worth carrying forward. I wrote the S7 Swift
fixture from what I *assumed* SwiftPM emitted rather than from what it emits. It passed, and it was
wrong. All three collector fixtures are now verbatim excerpts of artefacts downloaded from a real
run. **A fixture that agrees with its author instead of with the tool is the same self-agreement
defect §5.2 is about — repeated by me, two slices after recording it.**

One related gap fixed alongside: `"ts"` was missing from `isTestReference`, so a row backed only by
TypeScript tests would have skipped the executed-test check entirely and could have reached `tested`
on evidence nobody verified had run. No row currently depends on it.

### 5.2 The S5 self-agreement finding

**The most important defect found in WP-01, and the reason the harness exists.**

### What happened

S4b/S4c emitted the crypto vectors and a Go consumer verified them. Everything was green. It was
green for the wrong reason.

The vector files **were not self-contained**:

- `ratchet_sequences.json` recorded no private keys.
- `x3dh_kat.json` recorded only the **public** halves of the key material.

The Go consumer could not have reproduced the expected bytes from the file alone — so it didn't. It
**re-derived the generator's own seeds** and computed the same values the generator had computed,
by running the same code. The test proved that `vectorgen` agrees with itself.

### Why that is worse than a failing test

The entire purpose of a golden-vector suite (TRS §18.4) is that an **independent implementation**
reproduces exact bytes. A vector a second implementation cannot consume is not a vector; it is a
snapshot of one implementation's opinion. Java and Swift would have hit this the moment they tried
to consume the files — and if the files had been "fixed" by handing those runners the same
re-derivation shortcut, all three languages would have agreed with each other while agreeing about
nothing.

This is the exact failure mode a cross-language conformance harness is built to prevent, and it had
been introduced by the harness's own author.

### Fix

- Vectors now record **`TESTONLY-` namespaced private material** and an explicit DH-turn key list —
  everything a consumer needs, in the file.
- The Go consumer was rewired to read the file and nothing else.
- Java and Swift were then written against the same files and reproduce the same bytes
  independently.

### Structural consequences kept

`tools/vectorgen/gen_test.go` asserts every emitted file carries `TESTONLY-` provenance, and
`.gitleaks.toml` carries a line-granularity rule that private material in `test-vectors/` must be
`testonly_`-prefixed in the **field name**.

### Related defects found the same way, all kept fixed

| Slice | Defect | Why it mattered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S6 | The trace gate ran **green while blind to Swift** (`swift: 0 passing tests`) — SwiftPM emits the xUnit report only with `--parallel`. | Fixed with the flag **and** structurally: `-collect` now **fails** when a declared source yields zero passing tests. A silent zero is indistinguishable from success. |
| S6 | `tracecheck -stamp` **silently deleted the top-level `owner_gates` register** because the `Matrix` struct did not model it. | Caught by diffing against HEAD before committing; restored from git. `TestMatrixStructCoversEveryTopLevelField` makes it impossible to repeat. |
| S6 | The collector mangled Java IDs — Gradle writes `@DisplayName` into the XML `name` attribute and the Swift-oriented trimming took the last word. | IDs matched no matrix row, so the gate went quiet rather than red. |
| S7 | The collector preferred `classname` over the suite name; `node:test` writes the literal `classname="test"` for every case. | Would have collapsed the admin module into identifiers beginning `test.` — again quiet, not red. First test coverage for the collector, with a real fixture per runner. |
| S7 | `repolint` flagged git-ignored build output as layout drift. | Any developer who had run `./gradlew` saw a spurious failure. A gate that cries wolf stops being read. |
| S7 | I claimed the secret scan was reading a truncated history (10 of 23 commits) and "fixed" it. **The diagnosis was wrong.** | `checkout` already fetches all heads; merged PR branches are auto-deleted, so ten *was* the whole history and my 23 were stale local refs. Corrected in `b0ca0f1`; both commits kept, because the sequence is the useful record. |
| Closeout | The collector preferred the suite name; SwiftPM's placeholder is on that field. **Every Swift identifier matched nothing.** | §5.1. Fourth occurrence of the quiet-failure shape, and the one that finally produced a structural rule instead of a point fix. |
| Closeout | `tracecheck -stamp -auto` read only the **uncommitted** working tree while the freshness check compares `base..head`. | The gate failed with a remedy line naming that exact command, and running it reported "nothing to stamp". A gate whose advice does nothing teaches the reader that the gate is broken rather than that they are. `-auto` now takes `-base`. |

### 6.2 In-scope requirements left `not_started`

Destinations marked **stated** come from the requirement text or an EDP work-package brief.
Destinations marked *inferred* are my reading of subject matter — **the EDP does not assign these
IDs to a work package by ID**, and the owner should confirm them.

| ID | P | Subject | Destination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TRS-PROTO-008 | P0 | Optional negotiated compression, decompression-bomb protection | **WP-06** negotiation + **WP-11** fuzzing — *inferred*; WP-11's scope names "fuzz campaigns on every decoder/parser … decompression" |
| TRS-PROTO-010 | P0 | Fragmentation independent of framing; reassembly timeout, duplicate suppression | **WP-06** — *inferred*; its constants (`REASSEMBLY_TIMEOUT`, `LAN_CHUNK_PAYLOAD`) are transport |
| TRS-PROTO-012 | P0 | Mesh forwarding authenticates TTL/hop/message ID; relay may not increase them | **WP-06** — **stated**; its brief names "mesh relay rules (TTL/hop decrement, drop policy)" |
| TRS-PROTO-016 | P1 | Semantic versioning + compatibility review for protocol changes | **WP-11** — *inferred*; release-gate work |
| TRS-CONST-004 | P1 | Calibration values tuned on reference device classes, evidence in `/evidence` | **WP-03 / WP-07** — **stated in the requirement text** |
| TRS-CONST-006 | P1 | Signed config selects predefined environment profiles (normal, crowded-venue, battery-saver) | **WP-08** — *inferred*; ADR-006 attributes config-override work to WP-08 |
| TRS-REP-008 | P1 | ADRs, threat model, privacy data map, generated API/protocol docs | **Partly done, no owner**: ADRs exist (9 of them). Threat model, privacy data map and generated docs are unstarted — *inferred* **WP-11** |

### 6.3 Deliberately not claimed

| Claim | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| TRS-CODE-006 (zero-warning static-analysis stack) — left `not_started` | It names a **five-tool** stack. ESLint + tsc strict and Android Lint `warningsAsErrors` are wired; golangci-lint, Checkstyle/SpotBugs and SwiftLint are not. A partial gate is not the gate, and `not_started` with nothing linked is what the honesty rule enforces. |
| TRS-CICD-004 (signed release artefacts + checksums + SBOM + provenance) — left `not_started` | Only an **SBOM stub** exists, and it declares its own incompleteness in its own metadata: direct dependencies only, no transitive closure, no provenance. Signing is owner-gated (G-05). |
| BLE / radio interoperability | Never claimed. No radio code exists. G-01. |
| Store approval, load results, legal or security sign-off | Never claimed. Owner-executed. |
| Swift verified on the authoring host | Not possible — Windows. Every Swift result in this closeout comes from a `macos-latest` runner, and the iOS shell had **never been compiled anywhere** until the S7 CI run. |

## 7. What WP-02 inherits

- Ten TRS §4.1 roots; 306 frozen constants with a pinned `constants_hash` and a frozen 128-bit
  service UUID; 14 generated artefacts across Go, Java and Swift — **no hand-written constant
  anywhere**, enforced by `lumoslint`.
- The complete §18.4 vector suite with a determinism self-check, consumed identically by four
  runners.
- A traceability gate that fails on incompleteness, staleness or a dishonest status — including a
  `tested` row whose test did not execute in the same run.
- A PR pipeline running all six TRS-CICD-001 stages, plus four empty shells that compile and lint
  clean from a container that has never seen the repository.
- Bootstrap scripts and a deterministic sample environment for a fresh machine.

**Entry criteria for WP-02 that this work package does not satisfy** and that are not its job:
physical devices for the WP-03 evidence loop, owner cloud/push projects for WP-05, and the
owner-commissioned cryptographic review behind G-07.
